title: Wild footage of cyclist and bus driver's verbal stoush at one of Adelaide's busiest intersections
text:
7NEWS brings you the latest local news from Australia and around the world. Stay up to date with all of the breaking sport, politics, entertainment, finance, weather and business headlines. Today's news, live updates & all the latest breaking stories from 7NEWS.
Wild footage of a road rage incident between a cyclist and bus driver has been captured by a 7 NEWS crew moments before they were due to go live to air. Sunrise reporter Hayden Nelson was moments away from reporting on Thursday’s cricket ODI between Australia and India at Adelaide Oval when he “heard this verballing” about 8am.
WATCH ABOVE: 7NEWS crew captures wild footage of road rage incident. Cameras then quickly focused on the verbal altercation between the cyclist and bus driver at the busy intersection of King William Rd and War Memorial Dr. The footage shows the pair angrily pointing at each other before the cyclist took off and stopped in front of the bus. After a chorus of honking horns, the bus then appears to hit the back wheel of the bicycle. The cyclist then lays his bicycle on the ground and throws his hands up in the air, as if in confusion, toward the front of the bus. He was then seen standing in front of the vehicle with his hands up, seemingly filming with his phone, as the bus then drove into the busy intersection. The cyclist, named only as Phil, told Sunrise the altercation was sparked by the bus overtaking him further up War Memorial Drive. “I was riding along down here, doing a good speed, he’s gone to overtake me and it’s been very, very close,” he said. “As he’s gone past I’ve seen there’s a lot of road on the other side of his bus ... I’ve come down here and banged on his window to get his attention and go ‘Hey, you could have moved over’.” Nelson reported police had been notified. South Australian Police later said the 54-year-old cyclist was not injured and investigations into what happened were continuing. “The bus initially stopped and the driver, a 62-year-old man, spoke to the cyclist before leaving,” SAPOL said. “Police have spoken to the company involved who are co-operating with the investigation.” Anyone who witnessed or has footage of the incident has been urged to contact Crime Stoppers.
